clue.text: Kind of ball fashioned around square, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters come out in an unusual order
around says one word wraps itself about the other

blocks.note: fashioned means made or formed
the letters of square, rearranged

explanation.surface: A ball designed, rather strangely, around a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters of square, but here it means the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a ball where guests wear masks, so it is a type of dance party.

clue.text: Get engaged repeatedly in schemes Holmes hatched

blocks.note: sits across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting caught up in plots the detective Sherlock Holmes devised.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of schemes and the start of Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear wheels are said to mesh when their teeth interlock, engaging over and over as they turn.

clue.text: It's used for opening act in theatre

blocks.note: surface reading: the first act on stage at a playhouse

blocks.clueFragment: It's used for opening act in theatre
blocks.note: setter's reading: a tool for cutting someone open in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' looks like the stage, but it is the operating theatre, and the opening is an incision.

explanation.definitionFit: The UN is the international body of member states founded in 1945 to keep world peace.

clue.text: Organised party membership, initially unsystematic

a do is a party
first letter of membership

explanation.surface: A party's membership was arranged with no real system at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random follows no plan or method, which is what unsystematic describes.

explanation.definitionFit: A delusion is a mistaken belief, a kind of error of judgement or perception.

clue.text: Appear in place of bishop, taking mass

clue.text: I'll feature prominently in his speech

blocks.note: setter's reading: the word 'I' crops up constantly when this self-obsessed person talks

explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' seems to be the speaker of the clue, but it is the first-person pronoun that a self-centred talker overuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceited person talks about himself all the time, so 'I' dominates everything he says.

clue.text: Like those in charge, chap set over African country shifting left

Algeria, with its L moved to the end

explanation.definitionFit: Managerial describes managers, the people who run and direct an organisation.

clue.text: HQ for force in Waterloo, say

explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle and force an army, but it is the London railway terminus and a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A police station is a local force's base, and Waterloo is a big railway stop in London.

clue.text: Poke fun at a politician in flier

taken as written

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
